advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the MCP SDK entrypoint name/signature: use `streamablehttp_client(base_url, headers={'Authorization': bearer})` (or the SDK's actual client factory) rather than `streamable_http_client(base_url, http_client=...)`.
evidence: No other test in the repo imports `streamable_http_client`; the existing auth/transport tests drive the ASGI app via Starlette `TestClient` instead (e.g. tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth.py:329) and never import an SDK streamable-http client — no precedent for this symbol/signature.

resolve_symbol could not confirm the `mcp` SDK in this environment (UNRESOLVED for both the underscored and non-underscored names), so this is a signature/name mismatch risk, not a proven non-existence.
advisory.finding: The always-runs read-tool oracle imports `streamable_http_client` from `mcp.client.streamable_http` and calls `streamable_http_client(base_url, http_client=http_client)`; the MCP Python SDK's Streamable-HTTP client is named `streamablehttp_client` and does not accept an `http_client=` keyword (it takes `headers=`, `timeout=`, `httpx_client_factory=`). If so, `test_committed_config_bearer_executes_read_tool` raises ImportError/TypeError at collection/run rather than exercising the transport.
scenarios: CI runs the always-runs oracle-1 parametrized test with the mcp SDK installed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify each committed config's env-var substitution against the client's actual expansion (or document that the always-run oracle only checks a test-side reimplementation, not the real client).
evidence: resolve_bearer + _expand_env: `return re.sub(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}|\$([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", repl, value)` handles BOTH $VAR and ${VAR}

test_committed_config_bearer_executes_read_tool: `bearer = resolve_bearer(client, subprocess_env())` then asserts `bearer == f"Bearer {TEST_PATS[client]}"` — the resolution is performed by the test, not the client under test

The real client substitution is only exercised in test_copilot_cli_loads_committed_config / test_codex_cli_loads_committed_config / test_claude_cli_loads_committed_config, each guarded by `@pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which(...) is None, ...)`

Named violating input: the copilot config commits `"Authorization": "Bearer $MCP_CLIENT_PAT_COPILOT"` (unbraced) while the claude config commits `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLAUDE}` (braced); if a client only expands one form, _expand_env still resolves both, so the always-run test stays green while the real client would fail.
advisory.finding: The always-run oracle re-derives the Authorization header with a test-side reimplementation of env-var substitution (_expand_env handling both $VAR and ${VAR}) rather than driving the real client, so a mismatch between a committed config's documented substitution syntax and what the real client actually expands is invisible when the client CLIs are absent (the CI-typical path).
scenarios: A committed config uses a substitution syntax the target client does not support, in an environment where that client CLI is not installed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen the codex CLI acceptance assertion to check the resolved server URL (as copilot/claude do) rather than only the echoed env-var name.
evidence: `assert PAT_ENV["codex"] in proc.stdout` — asserts the literal env var name MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX is echoed
By contrast the copilot/claude tests assert `EXPECTED_URL in proc.stdout` (line 321, 361)
codex config commits `bearer_token_env_var = "MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX"`; `codex mcp list` printing that name back proves nothing about resolution
advisory.finding: The codex CLI acceptance test asserts only that the env-var NAME string appears in stdout, which a config echo satisfies without proving codex resolved/consumed the bearer, a weaker oracle than the URL-presence check used for the copilot and claude CLI tests.
scenarios: codex lists the server but the bearer_token_env_var handling is broken.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the loopback server resolves REBAR_ROOT per tool call across threads (or set REBAR_ROOT before the fixture starts the server) so the seeded-store assertion is deterministic.
evidence: tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py:194-197: server app built and thread started in the module fixture before REBAR_ROOT is set
tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py:238-240: `monkeypatch.setenv("REBAR_ROOT", store)` … `rebar.config.reset_config_cache()` executed on the test thread
src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:295: the tool calls `rebar.list_tickets(...)` with no explicit `repo_root`, so it depends on ambient env/config resolution at request time in the server thread
dropped.finding: The module-scoped `live_server` fixture builds and starts the server before any `REBAR_ROOT` is set, and per-test store targeting relies on `monkeypatch.setenv('REBAR_ROOT', store)` inside `test_committed_config_bearer_executes_read_tool` being observed by the server running in a separate daemon thread. `reset_config_cache()` is invoked from the test (main) thread, but the server thread services the request; if the tool's config/root resolution caches per-thread or was already warmed at initialize, the seeded-ticket assertion may read the wrong store.
scenarios: Config or tracker resolution is cached at first request / per-thread rather than re-read from os.environ on each tool call.
